svg.title: One scalar, one code pair, two approximate views
svg.desc: One BF16 scalar x is quantized to one four-bit coarse code c and one signed four-bit refinement r. The same operation applies to every scalar in a vector of arbitrary length. Draft reconstruction uses c; verification reconstructs the same scalar using c and r. BF16 scale delta and minimum m are shared by 128 scalar values. The storage boxes show the logical codes for this one scalar, abstracting physical byte packing: two adjacent-channel fields share a byte within each code plane, and signed r is physically stored with a bias of eight. Matched reconstruction tracks compare the coarse and refined views with the original x. The visual example is x=6.28125, m=0, delta=1, c=6 and r=4. Quantization rounds to nearest with ties to even and clips using stored BF16 metadata; reconstruction is FP32 followed by BF16 conversion inside attention. The BF16 datatype does not restore precision lost to quantization.
